title: A map from a finite free module landing in the image of another lifts along it

standard_prerequisites.name: A basis of the finite free module
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the first line of the counted proof (line 600)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the construction of the lifting map to a choice on the finitely many basis vectors.

standard_prerequisites.name: Preimages under a surjection onto the image
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The hypothesis that the image of alpha lies in the image of beta, used at proof lines 601-602
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, for each basis vector, an element of N mapping to its image under alpha.

core_obligations: Choose preimages: for each basis vector e_i pick x_i in N with alpha(e_i) = beta(x_i), possible because the image of alpha is contained in the image of beta (proof lines 600-602).

Define the lifting map on the basis by linearity, sending a_1, ..., a_n to the sum of a_i x_i, and check that beta composed with it reproduces alpha on each basis vector and hence everywhere (proof lines 602-604).
proof_roadmap: Lift the finitely many basis images and extend linearly (proof lines 599-603).
Verify the resulting map composes with beta to alpha (proof lines 603-605).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for module maps alpha from a finite free module and beta into M, with the image of alpha contained in the image of beta, alpha factors as beta composed with a map into N (statement lines 591-597). The proof does not use any projectivity argument or the universal property of free modules in the abstract: it writes the basis e_i, chooses a preimage x_i of alpha(e_i) under beta, and defines the lifting map by linearity, checking the identity on basis vectors (proof lines 599-605). The point that makes this work is precisely that only finitely many choices are needed, which is the finiteness in the source. H2.
